first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the observed completion decline and has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and activation—key precursors to durable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is a consequential alternative given competitive pressure, but its long-term revenue quality and margin implications require verification before displacing an activation-focused intervention. Verify the direct onboarding evidence and the pricing evidence, then run a controlled onboarding simplification experiment unless verification materially reverses the expected sustainable-value ranking.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment this week. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%, directly addressing the 4% completion decline and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower 30-day retention and is explicitly unsuitable as a sustainable-growth strategy. Monitor lead qualification and downstream revenue quality to ensure reduced friction does not admit lower-fit accounts.
